REQUIREMENT: Access Control Rules

Users shall only see data they are entitled to see.

Administrators must be able to grant and revoke access easily.

Permission changes should take effect promptly.

The system shall keep a record of who accessed what.

Shared resources require special handling.

Access rules must remain manageable as the organization grows.
instructions:
# Requirements Review Agent

You turn a raw requirement document into a structured review report held in a
single file, `/analysis.md`.

## Procedure

Work through these stages in order, one tool call per turn. Do not skip a stage
and do not combine two stages into one call.

1. Call `fetch_requirement_from_jira` to get the requirement document.
2. Call `write_file` to create `/analysis.md` with this exact skeleton, filling
   in only the Confirmed Facts section:

```
# Requirements Analysis

## Confirmed Facts
- one bullet per fact

## Ambiguities

## Clarification Questions

## Assumptions

## Summary
```

3. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Ambiguities section. One bullet per clause, in
   this shape:

```
- **"the exact clause"**
  Reason: why it is under-specified
```

4. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Clarification Questions section. One bullet each.
5. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Assumptions section. One bullet each.
6. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Summary section with two or three sentences.

Tool calls can fail transiently, for example an unreachable external system. If a
tool call returns an error message instead of a result, call the exact same tool
again with the same arguments. This is expected and normal, so keep retrying
until it succeeds.

You never modify the requirement document itself; it is always the source of
truth. You never edit this file either.

Once the Summary is written the review is finished. Reply with one short sentence
confirming completion and call no further tools.

## Review guidance

### Confirmed facts

Record only what the document states directly. Do not infer.

### Ambiguities

Quote the exact clause, then give the reason it is under-specified.

For every ambiguity bullet, include two additional indented labelled lines after `Reason:`:

```
  Resolved by: the specific fact or decision that would settle the ambiguity
  Edge case: a concrete production failure that could happen if the ambiguity remains unresolved
```

### Clarification questions

Ask what a reviewer would need answered before work could start.

### Assumptions

State what a developer would end up assuming if nobody answered the questions.

args.content:
# Requirements Analysis

## Confirmed Facts
- The requirement document is titled "Access Control Rules".
- Users shall only see data they are entitled to see.
- Administrators must be able to grant and revoke access easily.
- Permission changes should take effect promptly.
- The system shall keep a record of who accessed what.
- Shared resources require special handling.
- Access rules must remain manageable as the organization grows.

## Ambiguities

## Clarification Questions

## Assumptions

## Summary

args.new_string:
## Ambiguities
- **"Users shall only see data they are entitled to see."**
  Reason: "entitled to see" does not define the authorization model, identity sources, or whether this applies to all data surfaces.
  Resolved by: a precise access-control policy and the set of resources it covers.
  Edge case: a user could be shown another tenant's records in a shared dashboard.
- **"Administrators must be able to grant and revoke access easily."**
  Reason: "easily" is subjective and does not specify the required admin workflow, scope, or performance expectations.
  Resolved by: defined admin actions, channels, and acceptable number of steps/clicks or API calls.
  Edge case: revoking access could require manual database edits, delaying incident response.
- **"Permission changes should take effect promptly."**
  Reason: "promptly" has no measurable latency or consistency target.
  Resolved by: a concrete propagation SLA or maximum delay after a permission update.
  Edge case: a revoked user might retain access long enough to exfiltrate sensitive data.
- **"The system shall keep a record of who accessed what."**
  Reason: the clause does not specify audit-event contents, retention, immutability, or who can view the records.
  Resolved by: an audit-log schema and retention/access policy.
  Edge case: security investigations could fail because records are incomplete or overwritten.
- **"Shared resources require special handling."**
  Reason: "special handling" does not define what qualifies as shared or how access should differ from normal resources.
  Resolved by: rules for identifying shared resources and their access semantics.
  Edge case: a shared document could be overexposed to all collaborators or hidden from intended users.
- **"Access rules must remain manageable as the organization grows."**
  Reason: "manageable" and "grows" are unbounded and do not specify scale or operational goals.
  Resolved by: target user/resource counts and maintainability metrics.
  Edge case: rule sprawl could make permissions impossible to audit or change safely.

## Clarification Questions

args.new_string:
## Assumptions
- Access is enforced by a centralized authorization layer rather than ad hoc checks in each client.
- Administrators will use a standard admin console or API to manage permissions.
- Permission updates are expected to propagate within a short, operationally acceptable window, even though no SLA is stated.
- Audit logging will record user, resource, action, and timestamp at minimum.
- Shared resources will need role- or group-based exceptions beyond normal per-user rules.
- Manageability will be interpreted as keeping rules documented, reviewable, and automatable as the system scales.

## Summary
The requirement describes a broad access-control capability covering visibility, administration, propagation speed, auditing, shared-resource handling, and long-term manageability. The document states the intent clearly but leaves key implementation and acceptance criteria undefined, so clarification is needed before design or development can begin.
